applicable_programme.grade_mapping_note: The public MYP page describes the programme as for students aged 11-16 and as a five-year programme that schools may shorten. Mapping Grade 6 (often about ages 11-12) onto the start of that span is our convention, not an IB grade or MYP-year boundary.

grade_specific_note.label: C
grade_specific_note.text: Grade 6 Florida ELA has no foundational-reading benchmarks and no ELA.6.C.1.1. Those absences are Florida’s grade list, not an MYP decision. Do not treat Grade 6 as a named MYP year.

official_requirements.text: The International Baccalaureate® (IB) Middle Years Programme (MYP) is for students aged 11-16.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: The MYP is a five-year programme, which can be implemented in a partnership between schools, or in several abbreviated (two, three or four year) formats.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Developing and applying these social, thinking, research, communication and self management skills helps students learn how to learn.

official_requirements.text: Using global contexts, MYP students develop an understanding of their common humanity and shared guardianship of the planet through developmentally appropriate explorations of: identities and relationships; personal and cultural expression; orientations in space and time; scientific and technical innovation; fairness and development; globalization and sustainability.

official_requirements.label: B
official_requirements.text: Inquiry is at the heart of MYP language learning, and aims to support students’ understanding by providing them with opportunities to independently and collaboratively investigate, take action and reflect on their learning.

official_requirements.text: MYP language and literature courses offer a study of a wide range of literary and non-literary text types, writing styles and techniques, allowing students to comment on the significance of any possible contexts, audiences, purpose, and the use of linguistic and literary devices.

official_requirements.text: The language and literature subject brief names four equally weighted assessment criteria: A Analysing; B Organizing; C Producing text; D Using language. The 1-8 band descriptors are not stored here.

typical_fit.label: C
typical_fit.text: Grade 6 Florida ELA in this draft asks students to analyze character interaction and plot, theme, shifts in narrator or point of view, and poetic form; to explain informational sections, central ideas, authors’ purposes, and arguments; to paraphrase and compare authors across time periods; and to identify rhetorical appeals. Students also write narratives, claims, and expository texts, follow grade-level conventions, research with multiple sources, and present orally. MYP language and literature uses the six skill areas and four criteria above. It does not assign those Florida sentences to a grade or to an MYP year.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.label: C

florida.alignment_note: Analyzing how character interaction contributes to plot can sit under criterion A Analysing and the example concept of perspective. The Florida plot demand is not an IB objective.
Explaining multiple narrators or shifts in point of view lines up with perspective as an example key concept. MYP does not require that narrator wording.
Tracking an argument and types of reasoning can connect to thinking skills and criterion A. Florida’s argument sequence is the state benchmark.
Identifying logos, ethos, and pathos is a Florida clarification under rhetorical appeals. The public MYP pages do not name those appeals.
Writing and supporting a claim fits criterion C Producing text. Florida’s evidence, elaboration, and transition rules are not printed as MYP criteria here.
Research that draws on multiple reliable and valid sources fits research skills. Florida’s reliability rule is the state benchmark, not an IB outcome.
Connotative and denotative meaning is a Florida vocabulary benchmark. The public MYP pages do not list that pair of terms.

suggested_alignment_to_florida_and_arizo.notes: Arizona standards deferred. These rows are suggested starting points (Label C), not an official IB-Florida crosswalk.
